## Solution

**Change of variables.** Let $u = g(x,y,z)$. By the change of variables formula,
$$\iiint_{g(S)} (2x+y-2z)\,dx\,dy\,dz = \iiint_S \bigl(2u_1+u_2-2u_3\bigr)\Big|_{u=g(x,y,z)}\cdot|\det J_g|\,dx\,dy\,dz.$$

**Jacobian.** With $g(x,y,z)=(3x+4z,\;2x-3z,\;x+3y)$,
$$J_g=\begin{pmatrix}3&0&4\\2&0&-3\\1&3&0\end{pmatrix}.$$
Expanding along column 2 (only entry $3$ at position $(3,2)$):
$$\det J_g = 3\cdot(-1)^{3+2}\det\begin{pmatrix}3&4\\2&-3\end{pmatrix}=3\cdot(-1)\cdot(-9-8)=3\cdot 17=51.$$
So $|\det J_g|=51$.

**Substitute the integrand.** With $u_1=3x+4z,\;u_2=2x-3z,\;u_3=x+3y$:
$$2u_1+u_2-2u_3=2(3x+4z)+(2x-3z)-2(x+3y)=6x-6y+5z.$$

Therefore
$$\text{LHS}=51\iiint_S(6x-6y+5z)\,dx\,dy\,dz.$$

**Evaluate over $S=[0,1]^3$.** Since $\int_0^1 t\,dt=\tfrac12$ and the other two variables integrate to $1$:
$$\iiint_S x=\iiint_S y=\iiint_S z=\frac12.$$
Hence
$$\iiint_S(6x-6y+5z)=6\cdot\tfrac12-6\cdot\tfrac12+5\cdot\tfrac12=\frac52.$$

So $\text{LHS}=51\cdot\tfrac52=\tfrac{255}{2}$.

**RHS.** $\displaystyle\alpha\iiint_S z\,dx\,dy\,dz=\alpha\cdot\tfrac12$.

**Equate:**
$$\frac{255}{2}=\alpha\cdot\frac12 \implies \alpha=255.$$
